topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture, recaps histopathology practical observations, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Discovery of transforming genes through tumour viruses and cellular assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the investigation of tumour viruses and in vitro transformation assays demonstrated that cancer-causing genes originate from misregulated normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Classifications and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer mutations and illustrate their operational mechanisms in cell cycle checkpoints and dominant-negative phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the distinctions, molecular repair failures, mitotic defects, and downstream cellular consequences associated with sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multi-step tumour progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how multi-step mutation models and inherited germline mutations drive the rate and dynamics of tumour development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to answer questions, and provides recommended reading.
